answer: Like a cedar that survives a gale only because its roots grip a ledge of solid rock, an agent economy should anchor each identity to one verified human sponsor. The sponsor stakes a small refundable deposit, may back exactly one agent per year, and must publicly re-confirm annually. If any sponsored agent is exposed as a sybil, the sponsor loses the deposit and can never sponsor again. One human, one identity, one yearly check: an attacker wanting thousands of fake agents must recruit thousands of real people, which makes large-scale forgery far costlier than any reward it could harvest.
